messages:
customer_acct: Hi — starting ~11:23 UTC our prod traffic to eu-west-1 started returning garbled tokens and some 401 errors. Outputs look tokenized differently (we see lots of broken subwords) and our invoice spiked. Request id: req-9a3f. Can you triage?

sophie_support: Sorry to hear that — we’ll take a look. Can you paste a minimal request + response (headers ok) and confirm you were targeting eu-west-1?

customer_acct: Yep. Minimal repro below (sanitized):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-customer-XXX" \
  -H "X-Redwood-Preferred-Region: eu-west-1" \
  -d '{"model":"rwdw-70b-v2","input":"Summarize: Hello world"}'
```
Response headers we received:
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json
X-Redwood-Served-Region: us-east-1
X-Redwood-Served-Model: rwdw-70b-standby-compact-vocab32
X-Redwood-Billing-Units: 8.3
```
Response body (truncated):
```
{"id":"resp-9a3f","output":"▁Hell o▁wor ld
Summar y: 
"}
```
This used to be a coherent one-line summary. Now words are split weirdly and we were billed ~8x more per request. Also saw intermittent 401s for ~10% of requests at the same time window.

sophie_support: Thanks, super helpful. Assigning to infra to confirm routing/failover behavior. @jared_infra can you check fallback logs for that time?

jared_infra: Looking. I pulled routing decisions for req-9a3f and a few neighbors. We see the customer header X-Redwood-Preferred-Region: eu-west-1, but routing service flagged capacity shortage and executed a failover policy. Decision log excerpt:
```
{ "req":"req-9a3f","target_region":"eu-west-1","available_capacity":0,"fallback":"region-standby","selected_variant":"rwdw-70b-standby-compact-vocab32","selected_region":"us-east-1","tokenizer":"bpe32","expected_tokenizer":"bpe50" }
```
So the standby variant has a different tokenizer config (vocab size 32 vs expected 50). That explains the subword splits. 401s look like auth probe failures that overlapped during the region switch (short-lived). Billing jump: standby_variant uses different billing units (8.3) vs active (1.0) — standby is actually more expensive here, likely because it's running a less-optimized kernel but bigger batching.

customer_acct: That tokenizer mismatch is surprising — failover should pick a compatible variant. Any idea why routing didn't check tokenizer compatibility?

jared_infra: Root cause appears to be a recent standby mapping change in commit abc1234: we added new compact weights to standby pool but forgot to tag tokenizer metadata. The fallback policy currently only checks architecture and seq_len compatibility, not tokenizer metadata.

anya_engineering: I can prepare a patch. Plan: (1) quick mitigation to pin this customer's traffic to the primary variant (no-failover) until we patch, (2) extend routing decision checks to include tokenizer.vocab_id and tokenizer.type, (3) add a monitoring alert to detect served_tokenizer != expected_tokenizer for prod traffic. PR #4821 created (draft).

nora_sre: For mitigation we can add a temporary customer tag to the routing-service: 
```
PATCH /v1/customers/customer-123/config
{ "no_failover": true, "pinned_variant": "rwdw-70b-v2" }
```
I can apply that now; will reduce risk but reduces availability during true regional outages. Also I’ll rollback the standby mapping to previous commit (abc1200) for the eu standby pool — scheduling a quick rollback window now.

customer_acct: Please do the pin ASAP — we need output fidelity for the app. Also want the 401s explained and a credit for the billing spike while this is investigated.

sophie_support: Understood. Nora — can you apply the pin and rollback? I'll open a billing credit request referencing this thread.

nora_sre: Applied pin at 2950001250 for customer-123. Rollback to abc1200 deployed to standby mapping at 2950001300. Deploy-bot: routing-service rollback to abc1200 successful (deploy id deploy-792).

deploy-bot: routing-service:rollback abc1200 — SUCCESS — 2950001300

jared_infra: After rollback and pin, I re-ran the same request. Headers now show:
```
X-Redwood-Served-Region: eu-west-1
X-Redwood-Served-Model: rwdw-70b-v2
X-Redwood-Billing-Units: 1.0
```
Output now matches expected tokenization. No 401s observed in the next 15m window.

anya_engineering: PR #4821 updated and marked for hotfix; will add tokenizer metadata checks to routing policy. Target patch deploy in next maintenance window.

sophie_support: I filed billing credit R-2026 for the customer for the affected window. Customer will get update via email when credit posts.

customer_acct: Thanks all, output looks good now. Please confirm fix timeline and whether you’ll add an automatic compatibility guard to prevent this class of failover.

anya_engineering: Confirmed — hotfix + added alerting. ETA for safety guard deploy: 48 hours. Will follow up in this thread with PR link and post-deploy validation results.

sophie_support: Marking as owner for customer comms. Will update once credit is applied and hotfix is live. :white_check_mark: 

customer_acct: Appreciate the fast response.
